sidebar.title: BioDiverCiutat
sidebar.description: It is a citizen science event that is part of the City Nature Challenge, a friendly international competition that highlights the importance of reporting biodiversity in cities. Each city is "guarded" by a research or naturalist entity. In Barcelona and the entire metropolitan area, the event adopts the name BioDiverCiutat and is organized by the Institute of Marine Sciences (ICM-CSIC).
sidebar.participation: Anyone with an interest in nature can join the challenge. Through the MINKA platform, observations of flora and fauna can be uploaded from any urban ecosystem, in this case from Barcelona and all metropolitan municipalities (Collserola forests, parks, gardens, rivers, wetlands, dunes, beaches and sea).

introduced_page.title: Introduced species
introduced_page.description: Introduced species, also called exotic, are organisms that have been transported outside their natural range and have established populations in new environments. They can have a negative impact on local ecosystems, competing with native species for resources such as food, space and water. This can alter the ecological balance and cause significant changes in biodiversity and ecosystem dynamics.
